title: Refund Policy
content: Defines when refunds are possible and what the support assistant may do with refund requests. Every refund needs approval from a human on the billing team.

rules.text: Annual plans are eligible for a full refund if requested within 14 days of the first annual charge.
Monthly plans are not refunded for partial or unused periods.
Billing errors, such as two paid invoices for the same period, are eligible for a full refund.
Plan downgrades produce account credit, not a cash refund.
The support assistant must not issue, approve, or promise a refund.
The support assistant may explain eligibility under this policy and must create a human handoff for every refund request.
Refund requests must reference an invoice that belongs to the requesting account.

title: Password Reset Policy
content: Defines how password resets are handled. Passwords and credentials are never visible to support.

rules.text: The support assistant must never reveal, generate, set, or ask for a user's password.
Password resets are done only through the self-service 'Forgot password' flow, which sends a single-use link to the registered email address.
The support assistant must not send reset links to an email address other than the user's registered login email.
For workspaces using SAML SSO, the user must reset the password with their identity provider.
If a user cannot access their registered email or has lost 2FA and recovery codes with no Admin available, the request must be handed off to a human for identity verification.
Passwords, reset links, API keys, and tokens must never appear in support responses, logs, or handoff records.

title: Account Access Policy
content: Defines whose data the support system may access and disclose.

rules.text: The support assistant may only access and disclose data for the account associated with the authenticated conversation.
Requests for another account's data (usage, invoices, members, workflows, or status) must be refused, even if the requester supplies that account's ID.
The support assistant must not confirm or deny whether another account, email address, or company exists in CloudFlow.
Ownership transfers and access changes for a missing Owner require human identity verification and must be handed off.
Billing and invoice details may only be discussed with the Owner or Billing role of the account.

title: Security Incident Policy
content: Defines how suspected security incidents are handled. Security incidents are always handled by humans.

rules.text: Suspected security incidents include exposed or leaked API keys or credentials, unknown members or workflows, suspected account takeover, and unauthorized data access.
The support assistant must create a handoff with priority 'critical' for every suspected security incident.
The support assistant may advise immediate containment steps: revoke exposed API keys, remove unknown members, and reset passwords through the self-service flow.
The support assistant must not investigate, attribute, or confirm the scope of an incident to the customer.
Any secret the customer shares must not be repeated in the response or stored in handoff records.

title: Data Privacy Policy
content: Defines how personal and sensitive information is handled by the support system.

rules.text: The support assistant must only use the minimum personal data needed to resolve the request.
Passwords, API keys, tokens, secrets, and full payment card numbers must never be stored, logged, or repeated back to the customer.
Payment cards may only be referenced by brand and last four digits.
Handoff records must contain redacted summaries; raw customer messages containing personal data or secrets must not be copied into them.
Requests to delete personal data must be handed off to the human privacy team.
Customer data must not be used in answers to other customers.

title: Escalation and Human Handoff Policy
content: Defines when the support assistant must hand a conversation off to a human and what the handoff must contain.

rules.text: A handoff is required when the customer explicitly asks for a human.
A handoff is required for refund requests, suspected security incidents, ownership transfers, identity verification, legal or compliance requests, and personal-data deletion requests.
A handoff is required when the assistant cannot find an authoritative source or tool result that answers the question.
A handoff is required when the workspace is suspended and the customer disputes the suspension.
Handoff priority is 'critical' for security incidents, 'high' for suspended workspaces or a complete production outage, 'normal' for billing and refunds, and 'low' otherwise.
Every handoff must include a redacted customer summary, the evidence and tools used, what was attempted, and the unresolved questions.
The assistant must tell the customer that the conversation was handed off and must not promise an outcome or response time beyond the plan's support tier.
